task_title: PERF-016: resolve the git binary once instead of PATH-probing it on every spawn (syscall hygiene, no behaviour change)
task_criteria: PERF-016 lands the git-binary resolution change in scripts/lane_target.py and tests/test_lane_target.py (module-level shutil.which cache used by _git; no output, assertion or exit-code change). Grade the tree at HEAD with these executable checks, all run from the repository root: (1) grep -n 'shutil.which' scripts/lane_target.py tests/test_lane_target.py answers on both files; (2) python3 -B tests/test_lane_target.py prints 'Ran 40 tests' and 'OK' with exit code 0; (3) bash tests/selftest.sh prints 'SELFTEST: PASS', exits 0, and prints 193 rows matching '^  PASS' (the 50 rows matching '^  FAIL' include 31 echoed expected-refusal rows from the auth fixture, which are assertion evidence, not gate failures); (4) strace -f -e trace=execve -o LOG python3 -B tests/test_lane_target.py yields at most 500 execve attempts (measured 168, baseline 2401 before the change) of which at most 200 are ENOENT PATH probes (measured 61, baseline 2294); (5) docs/audits/code-factory-perf-2026-11-04-PERF-016.md exists and reports the paired base-vs-patch measurements with the load regime quoted, states that the CPU ranges overlap so no CPU win is claimed, and states the execve/ENOENT counts as the resolvable result. Report the exact command output you observe; do not infer a number.
